description_full: Star Bulk Carriers Corp. provides international seaborne transportation services for dry bulk commodities. The company transports major bulk cargoes, including iron ore, minerals, and grain, as well as minor bulks such as bauxite, fertilizers, and steel products. The company owns a fleet of dry bulk vessels consisting of Newcastlemax, Capesize, Post Panamax, Kamsarmax, Ultramax, and Supramax vessels. Star Bulk Carriers Corp. was incorporated in 2006 and is based in Marousi, Greece.

financial_summary: Star Bulk Carriers Corp. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $3.3B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -10% over the past three years and +16% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +28.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 9% cost of capital — a 13-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $212M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.52× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
